one_liner: Senior supervisor of a Coast Guard contracting branch buying enterprise IT and cybersecurity, signing contracts as a warranted Contracting Officer up to unlimited dollar value.
fit_summary: This GS-14 role requires four or more years in contracting, a year at GS-13 level, FAC-C Professional or DAWIA Level III and 24 business-related semester hours. Daniel's contracting-related work is contractor-side proposals and purchasing at IEM, with no contracting certification and no supervision beyond a five-person intake center, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) under direct hire authority, so you don't need federal status, but you must meet minimum qualifications by November 5, 2026.

Positive education requirement: a bachelor's degree with at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, management, marketing, or related fields, with transcripts submitted at application.

At least 4 years of contracting experience, including 1 full year of specialized experience at the GS-13 level (e.g., pre-/post-award, negotiation, cost and price analysis, multi-million-dollar contracts); education cannot substitute.
FAC-C Professional or DAWIA Level III equivalent certification is required, plus the ability to sit for a warrant board for an unlimited warrant.
The posting lists a Q Access Authorization and requires a DHS background investigation; you must also pass the USA Hire assessment cut score.
strategy: Skip this one; the certification and contracting years are hard gates.

As a realistic alternative, search USAJOBS for GS-1102-07/09 contract specialist trainee roles open to the public, or FEMA and emergency management roles where his IEM experience is directly relevant.
resume_bullets: Found multimillion-dollar opportunities in SAM.gov and GovWin and led proposal writing (2019–2024).
Handled first-line IT troubleshooting with IT support at IEM (2019–2024).
interview_questions: Walk us through a complex, high-dollar acquisition you managed from requirement through closeout.
How do you set workload priorities and handle a subordinate whose contract files repeatedly have errors?
Describe a negotiation where you used cost or price analysis to reach a fair and reasonable price.
How would you brief senior leadership on a high-visibility protest or politically sensitive procurement?
watch_outs: Hard minimums (four years of contracting, FAC-C or DAWIA III, 24 business credits) are unmet on his resume.
Q Access Authorization and a DHS background investigation are required.
The position is fully on-site in Alexandria with no telework, which means a daily commute from Manassas.
